title: Independence from coordinate-free polynomial parts
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measured space, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be an independent family of real-valued functions, each measurable up to a null set. For a real coefficient family $F$ on subsets of the coordinates and a fixed coordinate $i$, form its coordinate-free part and its coordinate-derivative coefficient family as defined above. Then $X_i$ is independent of the pair consisting of the multilinear evaluations of those two coefficient families at $X$.
hypotheses_covered: $(\Omega,\mu)$ is a measurable space with a measure
Each coordinate function is measurable up to a null set
$F$ is a real coefficient family on coordinate subsets
replaced: Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ be a real multilinear polynomial and fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Define $A_i(x)=\sum_{S:i\notin S}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ and $D_i(x)=\sum_{S:i\notin S}a_{S\cup\{i\}}\prod_{j\in S}x_j$. If $(X_j)$ is an independent family of real functions on a measured space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and each $X_j$ is measurable up to a null set, then $X_i$ is independent of the joint pair $(A_i(X),D_i(X))$.
